title: What's Actually Covered Under an Interior Design Warranty? A Gurgaon Homeowner's Guide
author: Shivam Kumar

featuredImage.alt: Homeowner and designer reviewing an interior design warranty document in a finished Gurgaon apartment

keyTakeaways: An Interior Warranty Is Really Three Warranties — Your interior firm, the product manufacturers and your builder each stand behind a different part of the home.

contentHtml:
An interior design warranty in India usually covers manufacturing defects in modular furniture and workmanship defects in installation. Published policies range from about 3 to 10 years on modular kitchens and wardrobes, and up to 1 year on on-site work such as painting, false ceiling, electrical and plumbing. Wear and tear, water seepage, misuse and client-supplied items are normally excluded.

A warranty line appears on almost every interior quotation in Gurgaon. "10-year warranty" reads well until a wardrobe shutter bows in its second monsoon and you learn the number applied to something else. This guide explains what an interior design warranty in India normally covers, what it leaves out, and what to get in writing before you sign.

Key Takeaways

  • The headline number usually applies to modular products only. Site work often carries up to 1 year.
  • Three different parties stand behind your home: the interior firm, the product manufacturers and your builder.
  • Water seepage is a standard exclusion. In a new flat it is often the builder's responsibility under RERA.
  • A warranty is only as good as its written terms: start date, item-wise duration, exclusions and claim process.

An Interior Warranty Is Really Three Warranties

Most disputes start because the homeowner assumes there is one warranty. There are usually three, each with a different owner.

LayerWho stands behind itWhat it coversTypical duration
Workmanship (service) warrantyYour interior firmInstallation and site work done by the firm: carpentry fit, painting, false ceiling, electrical, plumbingUp to 1 year is common
Product warrantyInterior firm and/or the manufacturerManufacturing defects in modular units, hardware, lights and appliancesAbout 3 to 10 years on modular units; hardware and appliances as per brand
Builder’s defect liabilityYour developerStructural, workmanship and quality defects in the flat itself5 years from possession under Section 14(3) of RERA

In a turnkey interior project the first two sit with one accountable team. If you hire a designer and a separate contractor, they sit with different people, and each can point at the other.

What an Interior Design Warranty Typically Covers

The ranges below come from warranty policies that Indian interior firms and hardware brands publish. Your own contract is what counts, so treat these as a benchmark.

ItemWhat is usually coveredRange in published policies
Modular kitchen, wardrobes, storage unitsDefects in material or workmanship of carcass and shuttersAbout 3 to 10 years
Hinges, channels, drawer systemsFunctional failure of the fittingAs per hardware brand, often 10 years or more
Painting, false ceiling, electrical, plumbingDefects in workmanshipUp to 1 year
Sofas and loose furnitureFrame and structural defects1 to 3 years
Lights and appliancesManufacturing defects, handled through the brandAs per brand warranty card
Glass, mirrors, tilesChecked at handover; laying workmanship may be coveredOften no product warranty after handover

Hardware deserves a closer look. Hettich India's published schedule, for example, separates functional warranty from surface warranty. Several hinge ranges carry 10 or 20 years of functional cover but as little as 12 months on the surface finish. A rusted hinge in year three can fall outside warranty even though the hinge is "covered for 20 years". Brands revise these terms, so ask for the current document.

What Is Usually Not Covered

Exclusions matter more than the headline. These appear in most published policies:

  • Normal wear and tear: scratches, dents and fading from direct sunlight.
  • Water damage: seepage through walls, leaking pipes and flooding, including the damage they cause to paint, wallpaper, tiles and woodwork.
  • Pre-existing site conditions: damp walls, defective plaster or putty that the firm did not redo.
  • Misuse: overloading, physical damage or anything beyond normal domestic use.
  • Client-supplied items, and work altered by another contractor after handover.
  • Natural variation in wood grain and colour.
  • Glass and mirrors once accepted at handover.

Some policies also exclude rusting of metal parts, set a tolerance before a bent shutter counts as a defect, or suspend warranty support if the final payment is pending. None of this is hidden. It simply sits a few pages after the headline.

How to Read a "10-Year Warranty"

A long warranty is a good sign. Four questions tell you what it is worth:

  • Which items get the full term? In published policies the long term usually applies to modular and semi-modular products. Painting, false ceiling, electrical and plumbing commonly get up to 1 year.
  • Is it "flat" or "up to"? "Up to 10 years" means some items get less. Ask for the item-wise list.
  • What is the remedy? Most policies offer repair or replacement at the firm's discretion, not a refund.
  • Who do you call? One firm that handles the claim is different from being redirected to five brand helplines.

Compare these alongside price when you compare interior design quotations. A cheaper quote with a one-line warranty is not the same offer.

What Changes for a Gurgaon Home

New possession flats: check the builder first

Much of Gurgaon's interior work happens in newly handed-over towers on Dwarka Expressway and in New Gurgaon. Under Section 14(3) of RERA, a developer must rectify structural, workmanship and quality defects reported within five years of possession, within 30 days and at no charge. Seepage from an external wall or a wet area above is usually the builder's defect, not an interior warranty claim.

Before interior work begins, photograph existing damp patches and cracks and report them to the builder in writing. It keeps the responsibility clear later. Our Dwarka Expressway possession planning guide covers the full pre-work checklist.

Climate: the warranty will not save a wrong material

Gurgaon swings between dry summer heat and monsoon humidity, and wood-based boards respond to both. Because water damage is excluded almost everywhere, the board grade in kitchens and bathrooms matters more than the warranty term. See our guides on interior materials for Gurgaon's climate and plywood vs MDF vs particle board.

Older homes: scope decides coverage

In a 15 to 20 year old home in Sushant Lok or DLF, the firm can only warrant what it rebuilt. If old plumbing lines stay in place, a leak from them is not a workmanship defect. Decide the scope with that in mind. Our Sushant Lok renovation guide explains what is worth replacing.

10 Warranty Points to Get in Writing Before You Sign

  1. Start date. It should run from the handover date, not the order date.
  2. Item-wise duration. A table, not a single headline number.
  3. Brand and model of boards and hardware on the BOQ, with brand warranty cards handed over.
  4. Shutter warping, laminate peeling and edge banding. Are they covered, and is there a tolerance?
  5. On-site work. Is painting, false ceiling, electrical and plumbing covered, and for how long?
  6. Full exclusions list, especially water and seepage.
  7. Remedy. Repair, replacement or refund, and who decides.
  8. Claim process. Contact point, response time and any visit charges.
  9. What voids it. Third-party alterations, pending dues, change of use.
  10. Transfer. Does it pass to a buyer or tenant if you sell or let the home?

For the wider pre-signing checklist, see what's included in a full home interior design package.

How to Make a Warranty Claim

  1. Report the defect in writing, by email or WhatsApp, with dated photos.
  2. Quote your invoice or handover document and name the item.
  3. Allow a site inspection and ask for the finding in writing.
  4. Get the fix and the timeline confirmed in writing.
  5. If a valid claim is refused, send a written notice before escalating.

Interior work is a service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. A complaint must be filed within two years of the cause of action. The District Commission hears cases where the amount paid is up to ₹50 lakh, and the State Commission above ₹50 lakh and up to ₹2 crore. Complaints can be filed online through the e-Jagriti portal. This is general information, not legal advice.

How The Omega Group Approaches Post-Handover Support

The Omega Group runs design, procurement and site execution as one team, so there is one party to call after handover. On our projects:

  • Finishes, hardware and countertop materials are reviewed with you as physical samples or specification sheets before any order is placed.
  • Quality checks run through every milestone, 70+ on a typical project, followed by a handover walkthrough.
  • Hardware and modular components carry manufacturer-backed warranties, and our team remains reachable for post-handover questions or adjustments.

Warranty terms depend on the scope and materials you choose. Ask us for the item-wise terms for your home when you receive your quotation. Book a free consultation with our design team to discuss your project.

faqs.question: Do interior designers in India give a warranty?
faqs.answer: Most organised interior firms give a written warranty on modular furniture and on installation workmanship. Design-only consultants generally do not warrant work executed by a contractor you hired separately. Ask for the warranty document, not just the number on the quotation.

faqs.question: How long is the warranty on home interiors?
faqs.answer: Published policies in India range from about 3 to 10 years on modular kitchens and wardrobes, 1 to 3 years on sofas and loose furniture, and up to 1 year on on-site services such as painting, false ceiling, electrical and plumbing. Hardware and appliances follow the brand's own warranty.

faqs.question: Does an interior design warranty cover water seepage?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Seepage, leaking pipes and flooding are standard exclusions, along with the damage they cause to woodwork, paint and tiles. In a flat under five years from possession, seepage from the building is typically the developer's responsibility under RERA.

faqs.question: Is painting and false ceiling work covered?
faqs.answer: Only if the contract says so. Where on-site services are covered, the term is commonly up to 1 year and applies to workmanship defects, not to cracks or peeling caused by damp walls or structural movement.

faqs.question: What can void an interior design warranty?
faqs.answer: Common triggers are alterations by another contractor, misuse or overloading, use beyond normal domestic purposes, and in some policies an unpaid final instalment. Keep your invoice, handover document and brand warranty cards together.

faqs.question: Who fixes defects in a new flat, the builder or the interior firm?
faqs.answer: The builder is responsible for the structure and original construction for five years from possession under Section 14(3) of RERA. The interior firm is responsible for what it supplied and installed. Reporting existing defects to the builder before interior work starts keeps the line clear.

faqs.question: What can I do if a valid warranty claim is refused?
faqs.answer: Send a written notice with photos and your contract terms. If it remains unresolved, you can file a consumer complaint for deficiency in service within two years of the cause of action, online through the e-Jagriti portal.
